Question ID: GEO_U06_L01_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.CGM.8

Which evidence supports classifying a coordinate quadrilateral as a parallelogram?

answer.text: One diagonal is longer than one side

feedback.text: That comparison does not prove opposite sides are parallel.

answer.text: Both pairs of opposite sides have equal slopes

feedback.text: Equal slopes for both pairs of opposite sides support parallel opposite sides.
Appearance is not coordinate proof.
Every polygon perimeter is positive, so this does not classify the figure.

Question ID: GEO_U06_L01_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.CGM.8

Which calculation supports congruent sides in a coordinate proof?

feedback.text: Slope supports direction, not side length.
Midpoint supports bisection, not length equality by itself.
Area does not prove individual side congruence.
Distance calculations compare side lengths.

questiontext.text:

answer.text: The figure is always a square

feedback.text: A square requires more evidence than diagonal bisection.

Question ID: GEO_U06_L01_Q21

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.CGM.7

What is the midpoint of A(2, 6) and B(10, 14)?

feedback.text: Average the x-values and y-values separately: ((2+10)/2, (6+14)/2) = (6, 10).
This adds coordinates instead of averaging them.
This is not halfway between both endpoint coordinates.
This is the coordinate sum, not the midpoint.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U06_L01_Q22

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.CGM.7

Point P is 1/4 of the way from A(0, 0) to B(8, 12). What is P?

feedback.text: That is the midpoint, which is 1/2 of the way, not 1/4.
One fourth of the movement from A to B is (2, 3), so P = (2, 3).
That point is 3/4 of the way from A to B.
That is endpoint B, not a point 1/4 of the way from A.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U06_L01_Q23

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.CGM.7

Point P partitions AB in the ratio AP:PB = 2:3. If A(0, 0) and B(10, 0), what is P?

feedback.text: That is the midpoint. A 2:3 ratio is not an equal partition.
That point would be 3/5 of the way from A, not 2/5.
AP is 2 of 5 total parts, so P is 2/5 of the way from 0 to 10: x = 4.
The ratio gives parts of the segment, not the coordinates of P.

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.CGM.7

Which formula finds the point t of the way from A(x1, y1) to B(x2, y2)?

feedback.text: Adding endpoint coordinates does not create a weighted point.
This only works for the midpoint when t = 1/2.
This does not represent the fraction of the trip from A to B.
This weighted average starts at A when t=0 and reaches B when t=1.

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.CGM.7

A midpoint is best described as which kind of weighted average?

answer.text: An equal-weight average of the two endpoints

feedback.text: A midpoint gives each endpoint the same weight, so it is halfway between them.

answer.text: A point always closer to A

feedback.text: A midpoint is equally distant from both endpoints.
A midpoint lies on the segment between the endpoints.
Slope measures steepness; it does not locate the halfway point by itself.
